data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense via 'procedural rationality' merely shifts the inductive assumption from the level of the theory to the level of the methodology. To claim that subjecting theories to severe tests is a rationally justified procedure for 'pursuing truth,' one must assume the procedure itself is truth-conducive. If corroboration is strictly a non-predictive 'report card,' there is no logical basis to deem severe testing 'the only rational way to pursue truth' over any other arbitrary procedure. Asserting that the severe-testing procedure is truth-conducive requires the meta-inductive premise that this procedure reliably yields progress toward truth over time, an assumption that Popper's strictly anti-inductive framework cannot ground without contradiction.
